external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript app used by duty engineers to access dispatch operations and live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API used by the dispatch console and schedule importer.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet. CORS allowed origins and credential behavior are undocumented.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: A process that retrieves the scheduling partner's feed, parses XML, archives the document, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token that was issued when it was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder where the importer writes each downloaded scheduling document.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: The file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: load console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer loads the dispatch console from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin. Allowed origins and whether credentials are allowed are undocumented.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console maintains a WebSocket for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after it is open.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads from and writes to the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: publish planned work
data_flows.description: The scheduling partner publishes tomorrow's planned work to the schedule importer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML SOAP document

data_flows.name: write schedule archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls. It presents an API token.
data_flows.notes: The API token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers and the schedule importer are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: A same-company zone holding the live estate and greater operational authority.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: An account there can move a crew and change the work a depot does that day; a corporate laptop holds none of those rights.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The separate company that publishes planned work.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database's data is confidential because it contains job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and tokens or sessions.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents include personal information, business records, and credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The text identifies it as an API called by a browser-based console and used for cross-origin application requests.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule importer presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The text describes it as a batch importer that periodically pulls and parses a feed, rather than as a web application.
